newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela scraps Brazil refinery venture - PDVSA.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela scraps Brazil refinery venture - PDVSA.

text.p: Venezuela's state oil company PDVSA has decided not to build a new oil refinery in northern Brazil because the economics do not justify it, a top PDVSA executive said on Wednesday.

"We must agree that it doesn't make sense at this moment. However we are still looking at how to do business in Brazil," David Escojido, PDVSA's corporate planning coordinator, told Reuters in an interview.
"To build a grass-roots refinery today is too costly. It's better to get a refinery somewhere and add something to it."
Escojido said PDVSA, which owns 1.55 million barrels per day (bpd) of refining capacity outside Venezuela, planned to increase this to 2.1 million bpd by 2006.

"We are always looking for refineries wherever they are. That is true for the United States because its our main market, and the Caribbean and South America because the growth percentage-wise in the next ten years is enormous and we have to position ourselves."

He said PDVSA's acquisitive strategy, in sharp contrast to most international oil companies which have been selling and closing capacity due to poor returns, was to ensure a market for Venezuela's particularly heavy crude.
"We buy for strategic reasons. You need somewhere to land those heavy oils which are very difficult to sell," Escojido said.
But he added that PDVSA was unlikely to buy refineries in Asia because the transport costs were too high. "The transport would kill us. We cannot compete with the Arabs," he said.
